plate_findings.evidence: Caption: subcortical white matter lesions in the frontal lobe ipsilateral to the facial atrophy; white arrows.
Caption: cutaneous atrophy is visible and is marked by a white asterisk.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Patient axial FLAIR brain MRI demonstrates captioned ipsilateral frontal subcortical white matter lesions, a recognized imaging manifestation associated with Parry-Romberg syndrome. B: Patient coronal FLAIR MRI shows the captioned ipsilateral frontal white matter lesion and associated facial cutaneous atrophy in Parry-Romberg syndrome. Skin tone cannot be reliably assessed from the MRI.
panels.attribution_text: Turlea et al. Parry-Romberg Syndrome: Radioclinical Dissociation in a Paucisymptomatic Form and a Proposed Diagnostic Framework.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland) 2026. doi:10.3390/diagnostics16081219. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 5.
panels.figure_caption: Subcortical white matter lesions in the frontal lobe ipsilateral to the facial atrophy (white arrows), demonstrated on axial FLAIR (A) and coronal FLAIR (B) brain MRI sequences. Cutaneous atrophy is also visible in subfigure B (white asterisk).
in_text_mentions: Additionally, FLAIR sequences of the brain MRI demonstrated three subcortical white matter lesions within the left frontal lobe, measuring 4.02 mm, 2.3 mm, and 1.08 mm, respectively (Figure 5). Following administration of the contrast agent, none of the lesions demonstrated enhancement. Overall, contrast-enhanced brain MRI did not reveal any additional abnormalities. Furthermore, time-of-flight (TOF) arterial and venous sequences showed no evidence of cerebrovascular abnormalities.
